                  former colleague.

                  Mr Salmon pleaded guilty to one offence of forging 12

                  David Harbottle produced his pilot’s licence and log book
                  during a meeting with the CAA. The Certificate of
                  Revalidation entries for his MEP and IR ratings appeared
                  inauthentic. A forensic document expert found that the
                  entries were not genuine and the purported Examiner
                  confirmed that he had not made the entries. The false
                                                                                                                          Brighton
DAVID HARBOTTLE   revalidation entries meant that Harbottle’s pilot licence                            07/07/2021                          Fine £52,000
                                                                                                                      Magistrates’ Court
                  had not been valid on 7 flights.

                  Mr Harbottle was convicted after trial of two offences of
                  knowingly making a false entry in a pilot’s licence and
                  one offence of acting as pilot on 7 flights without an
                  appropriate licence.

CAA SUCCESSFUL PROSECUTIONS:
1 APRIL 2021 TO 31 MARCH 2022
DEFENDANT         BRIEF DESCRIPTION                                                                          DATE            COURT            SENTENCE

                  David Henderson organised a flight from Cardiff to
                  Nantes and back. The passenger was Emiliano Sala.
                  Mr Henderson was to be paid for the flights. He did not
                  hold the operator certificate or permit required for public
                  transport flights. Mr Henderson organised a pilot for the
                  flights who did not have a commercial pilot’s licence, a
                  rating to fly the aircraft type or to fly at night. The aircraft
DAVID HENDERSON   took-off from Nantes at night on the return flight and                                 12/11/2021     Cardiff Crown Court   18 months’
                  crashed into the Channel. Mr Sala died and the pilot was                                                                    imprisonment
                  not recovered.

                  Mr Henderson was convicted after trial of one offence of
                  recklessly or negligently endangering the aircraft and one
                  offence of attempting to discharge a passenger in the
                  UK.
                  Florin Olteanu was the pilot of a paramotor aircraft which
                  flew low repeatedly along the beach and seashore, at the
                  south of Hayling Island. He was warned by local Council
                  Community Safety Team that he was in breach of by-                                                      Portsmouth
FLORIN OLTEANU                                                                                           11/01/2022                           Fine £1,500
                  laws but he continued flying low in the area.                                                         Magistrates’ Court

                  Mr Olteanu was convicted after trial of six offences of low
                  flying.

1 APRIL 2021 TO 31 MARCH 2022
DEFENDANT              BRIEF DESCRIPTION                                                                         DATE            COURT           SENTENCE

                       As part of COVID-19 pandemic restrictions, Blue Air
                       Aviation SA was required to ensure that passengers
                       arriving in the UK on a Blue Air flight had completed a
                       Passenger Locator Form (PLF) and had a negative pre-
                       departure test result.                                                                                   Uxbridge
BLUE AIR AVIATION SA                                                                                         22/02/2022                          Fine £40,000
                                                                                                                            Magistrates’ Court
                       Blue Air pleaded guilty to five offences of failing to ensure
                       passengers had completed a PLF and one offence of
                       failing to ensure a passenger had a negative pre-
                       departure test result.
                       Craig Butfoy was a commercial pilot, who worked as a
                       First Officer. He applied for a job at two airlines,
                       providing false details about his flying experience and
                       qualifications and, as a consequence, was employed as
                       a Captain.                                                                                           Snaresbrook Crown    12 months’
CRAIG BUTFOY                                                                                                 28/03/2022
                                                                                                                                  Court          imprisonment
                       Mr Butfoy pleaded guilty to four charges of fraud by false
                       representation, one charge of making false entries in his
                       log book and one charge of intentionally altering entries
                       in his log book.
